properties.name: Arriving along the first fields
properties.why: Everyone arrives the same way: 3.5 km beside the agrivoltaic fields the city grew out of, then under one canopy where the coach stops and the city begins on foot. If arrival is a car park, the city has lied about what it is.

day.people: Field crews for the PV and jojoba shifts meet under the canopy; the arrival hall opens its cafe.
day.machines: Panel-cleaning robots finish their night pass on the trackers; the first driverless coach leaves for San Juan.

day.people: People from San Juan and the valley step off the coach and walk in on foot; children cycle along the alameda to school.
day.machines: Coaches and shuttles stop under the canopy; freight stays on the machine street to the cross-dock.

day.people: Visitors start at the arrival hall: the model of the city, guides, bikes for hire.
day.machines: Delivery robots take luggage to the guesthouse; the dock rebalances bicycles and charges drones.

day.people: The hottest hours: people wait under the canopy and in the hall, and walk in the shade of the poplars.
day.machines: The canopy's PV runs at its peak and charges the hub's batteries; fewer coaches run.

day.people: The market hall sells the fields' oil, nuts and vegetables; families meet arriving relatives on the square.
day.machines: Robots bring crates from the agri-processing yard to the stalls along the shared street.

day.people: The last coach; the square is lit low and warm, and the sky over the fields is kept dark.
day.machines: Freight moves only on the machine street; drones land at the dock for the night.

properties.render_note: Arrival by driverless electric coach on a straight road between the agrivoltaic fields (single-axis solar trackers over jojoba, rosemary and grazing alpacas) and a double row of tall Lombardy poplars with olive orchards; ahead, a long solar canopy over the coach stop, a two-storey arrival hall of rammed earth and timber, a market hall, people walking into the city with luggage and bicycles.

properties.name: A superblock of courtyard houses
properties.why: Housing is where heat, earthquakes, water and robots meet every day. If a family can live here in January and in a Zonda week without a car or an air-conditioner running all day, the rest of the city follows.

day.people: Windows open to let the night air through the courts; the first walks and the bakery on the corner.
day.machines: The night's deliveries wait at the drop point on the acequia street; no machine enters a lane.

day.people: Children walk in groups down the lanes to the kindergarten and the school.
day.machines: Machines on the nearby machine streets are held at the crossings at school time.

day.people: Shutters closed, lunch and siesta indoors; the bottom of each court stays in shade.
day.machines: Roof PV pergolas run at their peak and charge the block's batteries; robots wait in the shade.

day.people: People who work from home come out to the patio garden; neighbours share tools and food.
day.machines: Delivery robots bring parcels and groceries from the drop point to the doors at walking pace.

day.people: The patio garden is the cool place at dusk: play, dinners outside, the acequia running.
day.machines: The block's water is metered and the next day's channel flow is scheduled from it.

day.people: On a Zonda day families stay in the courts and the lanes, out of the north-west wind.
day.machines: Air intakes switch to filtered mode; panel cleaning is booked for the day after.

properties.render_note: Low courtyard houses two and three storeys high with thick walls in lime-washed render and rammed earth in warm whites and pale ochres, deep window reveals with timber shutters and lattice screens, roof terraces with solar panels and pergolas; shaded paved lanes with algarrobo and mulberry trees and a narrow open irrigation channel; children playing, neighbours at their doors, a small white delivery robot.

properties.name: Plaza del Agua: a square for 45 degrees and the Zonda
properties.why: A desert city needs one room where everyone can be outside at once. Here it has to work at 45 C and in a hot north-west wind, with water that is never wasted.

day.people: The market sets up under the canopy; older people walk the square before the heat.
day.machines: Robots bring produce from the cross-dock to the stalls; the acequia gate opens for the morning.

day.people: Classes and assemblies in the wind gallery; cafes fill along the north arcade.
day.machines: The canopy's PV feeds the arcade and the cultural hall.

day.people: At 45 C people sit under the canopy and in the grove; the sunken court is the coolest floor in the city.
day.machines: Water reaches the trees by drip at night, not now: only the basin runs, slowly.

day.people: The square is full: families, music, the market's second shift.
day.machines: Shuttles stop on the machine street at the north-west corner; robots keep to the shared streets.

day.people: Lights low under the canopy; the last cafes close.
day.machines: Cleaning robots sweep the square; the channel is flushed to the orchards.

day.people: In a Zonda people go down into the sunken court or behind the gallery; the market moves inside.
day.machines: Stall awnings are stowed; the basin is drained to keep dust out of the water.

properties.render_note: A large public square under a light steel solar canopy 9 m high casting dappled shade, a sunken court with stone steps and benches, a shallow stone water channel and basin, groves of algarrobo trees, a long arcaded three-storey hall on the west side acting as a wind wall, four-storey arcades with cafes along the north side; market stalls, families, older people on benches, people with bicycles.
